equity_bridge.item: Estimated H2 FY2026 owner FCF not yet in the 30-Jun-26 balance sheet
equity_bridge.note: FY2025 H2 reported FCF was $206M (746 - 540 H1); H2-26 assumed ~$180M on destocked Pool, less ~$15M H2 SBC. Estimate; replace with the FY2026 10-K cash balance at the next update.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case revenue path (judgment): equity CAGR rejected as unrepresentative
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (12.6-12.9%) diverges >30% from revenue CAGR (0.4% 3yr / 6.7% 5yr). Book value compounds from retained earnings and FY2022 Manitowoc Ice acquisition while revenue has been flat since FY2022; EPS growth came from margin expansion (80/20 transformation) and buybacks, not volume. Equity CAGR is not a usable growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC (withholding taxes not disclosed historically; FY2025 adds ~$11M). FY2020-25: 491, ~524, 253, 514, 653, 709 (FY2025 ex withholding). 3-yr FCF CAGR is inflated by the FY2022 trough (inventory build after the pool boom); the 5-yr ~7.6% is the meaningful figure. SBC is ~1% of revenue and not growing faster than FCF: owner-FCF and reported-FCF CAGRs are within 0.2pp. Revenue CAGRs: FY2020-22 pool boom then FY2022-25 flat at ~$4.1B.

scenario_narratives.base: Destocking is what management says it is: a one-season channel reset, not a demand break. Pool rebuilds toward ~$1.45B in FY2027 as dealer inventories normalise to sell-through, but higher rates keep new-pool construction subdued so the recovery is to the installed-base/aftermarket run-rate, not the 2021-22 boom. Flow and Water Solutions keep their 80/20-driven record margins and grow with price plus modest volume. Group pre-SBC EBITDA returns to a ~25.5% mid-cycle by FY2029. Taco is assumed to earn roughly its cost of capital and is excluded.
scenario_narratives.bull: Pool snaps back hard in the 2027 season (easy comp, restocking on top of normal sell-through, variable-speed pump and automation mandates lifting ASPs) and Flow/Water Solutions extend record margins, taking group EBITDA to ~27% - near management's low-30s Pool return-on-sales ambition across the cycle. Revenue compounds 5-8% through FY2031 as water-scarcity and efficiency regulation drive replacement demand. The new CFO (ex-Fiserv/TE/Lennox) restores disclosure credibility and the multiple re-rates toward 16x FCF.
scenario_narratives.bear: The destocking was a symptom, not the disease: higher-for-longer rates, weak housing turnover and consumer stress keep pool sell-through soft, the large distributors (concentrated customer base) run structurally leaner inventories, and Pool never regains its FY2025 level. Revenue crawls 1-3%, Pool margin deleverage and tariff costs hold group EBITDA at 23-24%, and the class actions plus a second CFO change in a year keep the stock on a cyclical 12x exit multiple. Taco integration distracts management and adds leverage (not modelled, a further downside).

valuation_philosophy.summary: Mid-cycle owner-FCF valuation of standalone Pentair through a Pool destocking trough. The market price sits near the 52-week low after a ~54% fall from the high; the question is whether FY2026 is a cyclical trough (base) or a reset to a lower earnings base (bear). SBC (~1% of revenue) is immaterial, so the house/street band is narrow and the valuation turns on Pool normalisation and the exit multiple, not accounting regime.
key_risks_to_valuation: Pool destocking proves to be weak end demand (rates, housing turnover) rather than a one-season channel reset
Taco ($1.425B, ~10.5x synergised EBITDA) is excluded; overpayment or integration failure would subtract value, and the $1.4B term-loan funding roughly doubles net debt on close
Securities class actions (Apr-Jul 2026 class period) - liability unquantified, not in the bridge
Tariff and input-cost inflation; the Q2-26 $35M tariff refund is excluded from the margin anchor
Terminal value capped at 14x FCF; ~half of EV sits in the terminal value

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY0 = FY2026E: midpoint of the cut FY2026 sales guidance $3.884B-$4.009B (Q2-26 earnings, 2026-07-28). Using the guided year as FY0 rather than FY2025 actual avoids counting H1-26 FCF twice (it is already inside the 30-Jun-26 net debt); the un-banked H2-26 FCF is added explicitly in the equity bridge.
inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted: 159.6M ordinary shares outstanding at 30-Jun-26 (Q2-26 10-Q statement of equity) + 0.8M dilutive options/RSUs/PSUs (Q2-26 EPS note). Held FLAT because SBC (incl. equity-award withholding) is expensed in the flows.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow add-back $37.0M (XBRL ShareBasedCompensation) + ~$11M estimated cash tax on net-share settlement (not XBRL-tagged; Q1-26 equity statement shows $11.3M 'shares surrendered by employees to pay taxes', concentrated in Q1 vesting, used as the annual proxy). Pentair publishes no combined figure. Interest income 0: the company is net debt.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases $225.0M; H1-2026 $348.2M (Q2-26 10-Q cash-flow statement). A real repurchaser: the flat count is funded.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD build: 10y UST ~4.3%, ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.1 -> cost of equity ~9.8%; pre-tax debt ~5.3% (term loans/senior notes), ~4.4% after tax; market-value debt weight ~16% (1.6B debt vs ~8.5B equity) -> ~9.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: Pool cyclicality, the governance/litigation overhang and housing sensitivity are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not by a premium (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842: operating-lease cost is already inside operating income/EBITDA, so lease liabilities ($127.3M at FY2025) are EXCLUDED from net debt. One treatment (B), no double charge.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (routing table: US operating company, cyclical industrial -> owner-fcf.md + adaptations (risk-once, WC sign, lease treatment)). First valuation of PNR (no memory entry). MID-CYCLE NORMALISATION: FY2026 is a trough year for Pool (channel destocking ~$250M sales hit; Q2-26 Pool sales -42%, segment margin 23.4% vs 35.7%) while Flow (26.5% ROS) and Water Solutions run at records. The growth path rebuilds Pool toward management's ~$1.45B FY2027 recovery figure and the margin path returns pre-SBC EBITDA to a ~25.5% mid-cycle level (FY2025 underlying ~26-27% after one-off impairments, keeping ~1pt of recurring restructuring/transformation inside). The Q2-26 $35M tariff refund is treated as non-recurring and excluded from the margin anchor. TACO: the $1.425B Taco Group acquisition (~$540M revenue, ~10.5x FY26 EBITDA incl. synergies, to be funded by a $1.4B term loan, expected Q4-26) is NOT modelled - valued STANDALONE on the premise that a deal at ~fair value is roughly NPV-neutral; neither Taco's flows nor the $1.4B of acquisition debt are included. Once it closes the next update must add both together. Net debt = total debt $1,606.0M (all long-term, carrying value) - cash $91.8M at 30-Jun-26. Working capital capture is NEGATIVE (manufacturer: receivables+inventory ~$1.15B vs payables): growth consumes cash. Securities class actions (filed Sept-26) are unquantified and not in the bridge.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 +5.5%: Pool rebuilds from ~$1.30B toward management's ~$1.45B recovery figure (+~$120M) plus ~4% core growth (price ~3% + volume) in Flow/Water Solutions; decelerates to GDP-plus 2.5-3.5%. FY2022-25 revenue was flat, so a 10-yr ~3.7% average is not a stretch but is not a boom either.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC EBITDA: FY2025 GAAP EBITDA 23.4% + SBC 0.9% + one-off impairments 1.1% = ~25.4%, with ~2pts of restructuring/transformation inside; FY2026E adjusted ~26.5% ex the $35M tariff refund. Mid-cycle 25.5% keeps ~1.5pt of recurring restructuring/transformation and caps the projected owner-FCF margin near 18% against 16.0-17.0% achieved in FY2024-25 (cash tax was only ~10% in FY2025). FY2027 24.8% because Pool volume deleverage unwinds over two seasons.
base.da_rationale: FY2025 D&A $117.7M (59.6 depreciation + 58.1 acquired-intangible amortization) = 2.8%; amortization rolls off toward depreciation ~1.5-2%. Only affects cash tax.
base.capex_rationale: FY2025 1.65%, FY2024 1.8%, H1-26 1.9% (Pool capex up). Asset-light assembler.
base.tax_rationale: Irish-domiciled; FY2025 cash taxes paid $86.9M (~10-11% of EBIT), FY2022-24 ~$120M (~15-17%); GAAP ETR 12.5-14%. Pillar Two 15% minimum lifts the cash rate to 16-17%.
base.wc_rationale: NWC (AR 483 + inventory 666 - payables) ~20%+ of sales; charge 15% of each revenue increase.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: management's inventory visibility has just been shown to be poor (guide cut within one quarter, CFO exit, securities class actions), the Pool customer base is concentrated, and leverage rises with Taco. Base 50%: the evidence (Flow/WS records, price realisation +5% in Pool even in Q2) supports a transient channel event. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs a sharp Pool rebound AND further margin expansion AND a credibility re-rate, three independent things.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
